subject: economics
title: Rostow and Lewis Models
welcome_lead: Two classic development models - stages and dual sectors.
meta_desc: A-Level Development: Rostow's stages and Lewis dual-sector model.
final_note: Industrialisation pulls labour from low-productivity farming to high-productivity industry.

concepts.def: Walt Rostow - five stages of growth.
Rostow's third stage - rapid industrial growth.
Dual sector - traditional agriculture and modern industry.
Shift of labour from farming to industry and services.

walkthroughs.body_html: Rostow's stages - traditional, preconditions, take-off, drive to maturity, age of high mass consumption - describe a linear path that not all countries follow.
The Lewis model moves surplus labour from agriculture to industry. Industrial wages stay flat while surplus exists, then rise - the Lewis turning point - as labour becomes scarce.
China's 30-year boom from 1980 mirrored the Lewis story. Its turning point arrived around 2010 - wages began rising rapidly as rural surplus thinned.
